description: Our projects : making digital museum for students to show the importance of the discarded equipment in Moon and Mars by NASA. With simple and descriptive information, young generations may learn and be interested to all the discarded equipment and develop the future of the study of astronomy
summary: A digital museum which made to used by young generation (8-15). Images and videos make it more interesting. Cosmic Archive explains the equipment left in the Moon and the Mars by NASA dramatically.
details:
Cosmic Archive is an interactive digital space museum designed to help users explore the history and contributions of NASA's space exploration equipment on the Moon and Mars. Through an interactive presentation created using Genially, users can touch and explore different elements to learn about space exploration missions, including Surveyor 3, the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1), the Kepler Space Telescope, and the Sojourner Rover.

The main benefit of Cosmic Archive is that it makes learning about space exploration more engaging, accessible, and interactive. Instead of simply reading information from a textbook, users can actively explore the project and discover the scientific importance of different NASA missions. The intended impact is to increase people's interest in astronomy, space exploration, and scientific discoveries while helping them understand how past missions have contributed to our knowledge of space.

The project was developed using Genially, an interactive digital presentation platform. Its creativity comes from combining space-related information with an interactive digital museum experience, allowing users to explore NASA's historical equipment in a more engaging way. During development, the team considered the accuracy of scientific information, the accessibility of the content, the user experience, and the importance of presenting complex space exploration history in a clear and understandable manner.

Cosmic Archive aims to transform space education into an interactive experience that inspires curiosity about the universe and the future of space exploration.
